humanities_role_explanation: Historical newspaper articles (BLN600) supply the OCR/ground-truth pairs, but the competence tested is generic post-OCR text correction (character-level denoising), not disciplinary interpretation or historical knowledge.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: Text only: noisy OCR output is the input and manually re-keyed transcription is the target; page images are not given to the models.
analytical_tasks_explanation: Post-OCR correction framed as sequence-to-sequence / prompt-based 'Fix the OCR errors in the provided text'; error types analysed include substitutions, insertions, deletions, misnamed entities and hallucinations. No interpretive task.

general_purpose_benchmark.note: Single-task study on post-OCR correction of one corpus (BLN600); not a broad multi-task benchmark.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: Llama 2 7B and 13B (instruction-tuned with LoRA) compared with BART base/large.

quantitative_metrics.note: Percentage reduction in character error rate (CER).

summary: The paper instruction-tunes Llama 2 (7B, 13B) with LoRA for post-OCR correction of BLN600, a parallel corpus of 19th-century British newspaper articles, and compares it to fine-tuned BART. Llama 2 13B roughly halves CER and remains strong with little training data.
key_findings: Llama 2 13B reduces CER by 54.51% versus 23.30% for BART large; Llama 2 7B 43.26%, BART base 14.60%. Llama 2 performs well from the smallest training subset while BART improves with more data. Substitutions and deletions are easiest to correct; insertions and misnamed entities are harder.
evaluation_unit: sequence pair (OCR segment with ground-truth segment)
gold_upstream: BLN600 (Booth et al., 2024): parallel corpus of OCR text from British Library Newspapers with manually re-keyed human transcriptions; the paper does not describe further how the transcriptions were produced.
facets_explanation: Reference texts are the manually re-keyed human transcriptions in BLN600, a previously published corpus by overlapping authors; this paper treats them as a single ground truth and does not discuss annotator disagreement. Correction is judged against the OCR input and its surrounding context, so no outside knowledge is required by the key.
results_explanation: Table 3 reports 'Llama 2 13B 54.51' as CER reduction (%) as the best result, averaged over five runs; the metric is percentage reduction in CER, not raw CER, hence 'other'. The training-size comparison is across training set sizes (an ablation), not a format gap. No human baseline is reported.

humanities_role.quote: Poor OCR quality continues to be a major obstacle for humanities scholars seeking to make use of digitised primary sources such as historical newspapers.

primary_evaluation_setting.quote: By instruction-tuning Llama 2 and comparing it to a fine-tuned BART on BLN600

gold_source.quote: The dataset contains OCR text sourced from British Library Newspapers along with manually re-keyed human transcriptions.

gold_beyond_stimulus.quote: For each ground truth segment, the corresponding OCR text is then gathered using a search algorithm to create a dataset of source and target texts

answer_multiplicity.quote: computing the Levenshtein distance between the recognised text and the reference text and dividing it by the total number of characters in the reference text
